To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) 5-HTT overexpression in the mouse brain impairs fear conditioning and 2) 5-HT transporter overexpression reduces amygdala hemodynamics and theta frequency neuronal oscillations in this region.

increased 5-HTT gene expression in mice reduces fear learning and impairs the amygdala hemodynamics response and theta-frequency neuronal oscillations to aversive stimuli, suggesting that these neural processes are modulated by 5-HT.

(1) 5-HTT gene variation is associated with altered amygdala function; (2) the 5-HTTLPR gene variant is associated with altered neuronal oscillations and hemodynamic responses in the amygdala; and (3) the amygdala is a key structure in mediating fear learning, and the 5-HT transporter gene variation modulates fear learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms that underlie individual variation in brain function and behaviour.
the neural mechanisms that underpin the association between the 5-HTTLPR and anxiety.
understanding how the brain works, in particular, how it responds to stress and how this may be influenced by the genes we inherit.

5-HTT overexpression impairs fear learning, and this is associated with reduced amygdala responses and neuronal oscillations during fear conditioning.
the 5-HTTLPR polymorphism is associated with the risk of anxiety and depressive disorders.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
5-HTT modulates amygdala hemodynamics, which in turn may be mediated by theta frequency oscillations.
the amygdala is a key site of 5-HT modulation of emotional responses and that the effects of 5-HT on amygdala function are mediated in part by 5-HT modulation at the level of neuronal oscillations.
5-HTT gene variation modulates fear learning, hemodynamic responses, oscillations, and their interrelationships in the amygdala.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amygdala hemodynamics can be used to study the effects of 5-HT on fear learning and memory.
5-HTT genotype can modulate amygdala activity in a way that may underlie the effects of 5-HTTLPR variation on fear learning and anxiety-related traits.
variation in 5-HTT levels is likely to influence the neural circuitry of fear learning and fear expression in humans.
